native_mechanisms: A runner traverses each outgoing road and lays a candidate stick on the far heap whose length is the home heap's current ember plus that road's notch (edge relaxation by push).

All heaps throw their accumulated candidate sticks at once in one land-wide synchronized throw, and a single row read straight across all heaps simultaneously picks each heap's shortest candidate as its new ember while all longer candidates are discarded (materialized per-node candidate pools resolved by a global columnar/row-wise min).

A garrison permanently seals a heap once its ember is unchanged between consecutive throws, freezing its distance and permanently halting its outgoing runners; a heap never lit across throws is declared unreachable.
core_technique: CSR build, then round-synchronous frontier Bellman-Ford (stamped active set) with a work budget that hands over to binary-heap Dijkstra, plus a dense/small-n branch that is plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra with an AVX2 argmin.
